hook: "We are 87 days away from Black Friday." — countdown urgency for operators.
body: Q4 playbook bullets from @codyplof, @couuor + @connorrolain: reuse top creative from 2025, scale-up tests before BFCM, launch new products in October, pre-sales for non-hero SKUs, make decisions from aMER (post truncated).
idea: Q4 is won before November — reuse proven creative, finish testing early, launch new products in October, and pre-sell non-heroes while CPMs are still baseline.
sequencing: The countdown (87 days to BF)
The playbook sources (three operators)
The five moves: reuse winners → pre-BFCM scale tests → October launches → non-hero pre-sales → aMER decisions
The truncated tail (aMER point cut off — the 84s video holds the rest)
why_it_works: The countdown creates a ticking clock for a specific audience (media buyers), and the checklist format makes the episode feel actionable before watching.
what_to_steal: LC's Q4 checklist: lock winners by October, launch newness in October, pre-sell non-hero SKUs early, judge everything on aMER.

hook: "Most ecom founders are about to walk into Black Friday still hunting for their winning ads. Wrong move." — contrarian warning.
body: The sequence is imitate → ideate → test → find winners → scale — and it must happen BEFORE Black Friday: "You don't discover what works on the 27th. You should already" (post truncated).
idea: Winners must be found before BFCM, not during it — the testing sequence (imitate → ideate → test → winners → scale) has a deadline.
sequencing: The warning (founders hunting winners too late)
The verdict (wrong move)
The rule (know your winners now)
The sequence (imitate → ideate → test → winners → scale)
The deadline (not the 27th — already known)
why_it_works: "You don't discover what works on the 27th" is a quotable deadline — it turns a vague "test early" into a specific failure image.
what_to_steal: LC's creative-testing deadline: all BFCM winners locked by early November; the imitate → ideate → test pipeline starts now.

hook: "My Black Friday strategy on Meta is just leave on the ads you've had on all year." — deliberately boring advice.
body: The BF playbook: keep year-round winners running, add a second lifetime-budget campaign with the sale ads; on AppLovin, take top creatives, add a discount badge, update end cards with the offer + URL, leave on.
idea: Don't rebuild for Black Friday — keep proven creative running and layer the sale on top (new campaign, discount badge, updated end cards).
sequencing: The boring thesis (leave winners on)
The Meta layer (second lifetime-budget campaign with sale ads)
The AppLovin layer (discount badge + offer end cards + URL update)
The closer (leave on)
formatting: Short text post; 160 likes / 150 bookmarks — the most-saved in the folder.
why_it_works: "Just leave them on" is contrarian against the industry's rebuild-everything instinct — and it protects the learning/optimization the winners accumulated all year.
what_to_steal: LC's BF rule: year-round winners keep running; sale creative goes in a separate lifetime-budget campaign — never pause winners to launch BF variants.

hook: "How to add 30,000-50,000 new Email contacts to your list before BFCM" — specific list-growth promise.
body: September CPMs are still baseline; by mid-November CPMs spike past $80 as everyone bids the same audiences; the brands doing $1M+ over Cyber Week aren't (post truncated) — the implication is they build the list now, cheaply.
idea: List-building arbitrage: acquire emails in September at baseline CPMs before the mid-November $80+ CPM spike — the Cyber Week winners buy their audience early.
sequencing: The promise (30–50K new emails before BFCM)
The window (September = baseline CPMs)
The spike (mid-November, $80+ CPMs, same audiences)
The winners' behavior (truncated, implied: they build early)
why_it_works: The $80 CPM spike is a concrete, scary number with a date attached — it turns "build your list" from advice into an expiring arbitrage.
what_to_steal: LC's September/October list-build push: quiz, giveaway, and lead-magnet spend now while CPMs are baseline — the Cyber Week audience should be owned, not rented in November.

hook: "build a separate batch of creative just for the week after Black Friday." — counter-intuitive timing advice.
body: Brands pour everything into BF/CM then pull spend right after — but people are still shopping; 3 weeks of holiday gifting remain (post truncated).
idea: The week after Black Friday is an under-served window — competitors pull back while shoppers keep buying, so dedicated post-BF creative captures cheap, high-intent demand.
sequencing: The directive (separate creative batch for post-BF week)
The common mistake (all-in on BF/CM, then pullback)
The reality (people still shopping)
The window (3 weeks of gifting left, truncated)
why_it_works: Counters the industry's BFCM tunnel vision — it names a specific, neglected window where competition drops but intent stays high.
what_to_steal: LC's post-BFCM creative batch: "missed the sale?" gifting angles for the 3 weeks after Cyber Monday — competitors go quiet, LC stays loud.

body: Seasonality warning in parallel structure: the October winner might die in November; the BF winner might destroy margin in December; the gifting winner might fail in January — "seasonality changes buyer psychology. don't mistake temporary behavior" (truncated).
idea: Q4 winners are seasonal artifacts, not durable truths — buyer psychology shifts month to month, so don't mistake temporary behavior for a permanent read.
sequencing: The memo frame (Q4 reminder)
Check 1: October → November (ad dies)
Check 2: Black Friday → December (offer destroys margin)
Check 3: Gifting → January (creative fails)
The principle (seasonality changes buyer psychology)
formatting: Short text post; parallel-structure aphorisms, truncated.
why_it_works: The parallel "X might Y" rhythm makes each month's trap feel inevitable — it's a warning engineered to be remembered in the moment of over-scaling.
what_to_steal: LC's Q4 discipline: re-validate winners monthly; cap BF offer depth so December margin survives; don't carry gifting creative into January.

hook: "for Black Friday, swap your landing page and keep your winning creative running." — the inversion of the common mistake.
body: Brands do the opposite: pause year-round winners and launch brand-new BF videos with a big discount on screen — then the new ads "start from zero during" (truncated) the most expensive auction of the year.
idea: Swap the landing page, not the creative — new BF ads start from zero optimization in the year's priciest auction, while proven winners keep their learning.
sequencing: The rule (swap LP, keep creative)
The common mistake (pause winners, launch new BF videos)
The cost (new ads start from zero, truncated)
The truncation caveat (the auction-dynamics argument is cut off mid-sentence)
why_it_works: Pairs with the herrmanndigital post in this folder — two independent operators converging on "don't rebuild for BF" makes the principle feel consensus-grade.
what_to_steal: LC's BF execution: same winning creatives, sale landing page behind them — the discount lives on the page, not in a fresh ad.
